concepts.label: Ping (active health probe)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - an active, side-effecting health check that queries live services for status/latency; no existing registry concept covers SDK-side health probing

concepts.label: Diagnostics (passive health report)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - structurally distinct from sdk:ping: a passive, no-I/O snapshot of the SDK's already-known socket state rather than an active network probe

concepts.label: ClusterState enum (ONLINE / DEGRADED / OFFLINE)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the closed enum returned by DiagnosticsResult.state(), consumed by sdk:diagnostics

relations.subject: sdk:managing-connections
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate for a component observed through a named metric/endpoint/log surface
relations.evidence: `Ping` _actively_ queries the status of the specified services, giving status and latency information for every node reachable.

relations.subject: sdk:managing-connections
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate for a component observed through a named metric/endpoint/log surface
relations.evidence: `Diagnostics` shows what the SDK _perceives_ as the current state of the network and services — it is without side-effects, but may not be up to date.

relations.subject: sdk:diagnostics
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate for a documented output drawing its values from a controlled vocabulary
relations.evidence: A `DiagnosticsResult` has one interesting property over a ping result — it provides a cumulative `ClusterState` through the `state()` method. The state can be `ONLINE`, `DEGRADED` or `OFFLINE`.

relations.subject: sdk:ping
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted comparative predicate; ping is active/expensive/current, diagnostics is passive/cheap/possibly-stale
relations.evidence: Diagnostics works in a similar fashion to `ping` in the sense that it returns a report of how all the sockets/endpoints are doing, but the main difference is that it is passive.

relations.subject: sdk:diagnostics
relations.object: a binary yes/no answer about cluster health
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate for a stated, bounded non-support boundary
relations.evidence: This API does not provide binary yes/no answers about the health of the cluster; rather it summarizes as much information as possible, for the application developer to assemble a complete, contextual view and come to a conclusion.

notable_absence.finding: The Uses section lists third-party consumers of Ping/Diagnostics output (Splunk, ElasticSearch, Nagios, Kubernetes probes, Docker Health Check, AWS ELB), but the page never states whether Ping/Diagnostics results are also fed into the SDK's own observability stack (LoggingMeter, ThresholdLoggingTracer, OrphanReporter) documented elsewhere in this batch - the two families of mechanism are presented as entirely separate, with no cross-reference in either direction.

cross_product_finding: The page positions Diagnostics explicitly as the backing mechanism for third-party container/cloud health-check conventions that are not Couchbase products at all: 'Kubernetes Liveness and Readiness Probes', 'Docker Health Check with CLI commands', and 'AWS ELB through HTTP' - making this the SDK's most direct integration point with external cloud-infrastructure health-check tooling in this batch.
